question: What is the primary goal of a medical evacuation?

options.A: To provide permanent rehabilitation at the scene
options.B: To clear beds in overcrowded rural clinics
options.C: To reduce hospital admission costs for patients
options.D: To prevent clinical deterioration during transport

explanation: The core purpose of moving a patient medically is ensuring their condition does not worsen while traveling to a better-equipped facility. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h1)

question: How does MEDEVAC differ from standard patient transport services?

options.A: It only occurs during major national emergencies
options.B: No medical equipment is required inside the vehicle
options.C: Patients drive themselves to the nearest hospital
options.D: Specialized medical personnel accompany the patient

explanation: True medical evacuation involves dedicated clinical staff and monitoring gear inside the transit vehicle to manage emergencies en route. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h1)

question: A valid clinical reason for initiating a medical evacuation is...

options.A: the hospital running out of routine meal supplies
options.B: a shift change occurring among the nursing staff
options.C: unavailable specialty care at the current facility
options.D: the patient requesting a room with better views

explanation: Transferring a patient is justified when local clinicians lack the specific resources or specialties required to treat the illness properly. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h2)

question: A patient with severe head trauma is in a clinic without a CT scanner or surgeon. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.A: Discharge the patient home with oral pain relievers
options.B: Wait in the clinic until a visiting doctor arrives next week
options.C: Initiate evacuation to a tertiary neurosurgical centre
options.D: Keep monitoring vital signs locally without transfer plans

explanation: Lacking essential diagnostic and surgical capabilities makes rapid transfer to a facility with those resources vital for survival. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h2)

question: The primary framework used to prioritize and stabilize patients before transport is the...
explanation: Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, and Exposure form the universal baseline for emergency stabilization. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h3)

question: Why is pre-evacuation stabilization critical before starting a long road journey?

options.A: Transport drivers refuse to drive unstable people
options.B: Hospitals charge extra fees for unstabilized arrivals
options.C: The stress of movement can worsen untreated injuries
options.D: Medical insurance requires paperwork to be blank

explanation: Vibrations, motion, and altitude shifts during transit place physiological stress on the body, amplifying any uncorrected instability. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h3)

question: Which mode of medical evacuation is most commonly utilized for short distances in resource-limited settings?
explanation: Road ambulances are widely available and practical for connecting peripheral clinics to nearby secondary or tertiary centers. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h4)

question: What is a major limitation of using helicopters for medical evacuation?

options.B: High operating costs and weather sensitivity
options.C: Slow travel speeds compared to walking
options.D: Inability to carry any medical equipment

explanation: Helicopters are expensive to maintain and fly, and poor weather conditions like heavy storms or fog can ground them completely. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h4)

question: Why is physical assessment of a patient more difficult inside a moving ambulance?

options.A: Engine noise and vehicle vibration obscure findings
options.B: Lighting inside ambulances is always completely dark
options.C: Medical equipment automatically shuts down in motion
options.D: Nurses are legally forbidden to touch patients

explanation: Vibrations and sounds make auscultation with a stethoscope and visual inspection challenging during active transit. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h5)

question: A nurse checking an intravenous line during transit is primarily trying to prevent...

options.A: the patient from drinking the sterile water
options.D: freezing of the fluid bag from cabin air

explanation: Bumping and swaying on the road can easily pull cannula needles out of veins, interrupting vital fluid or drug delivery. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h5)

question: What key piece of information must the transport team constantly update the receiving hospital with?

options.D: Cost of fuel used for the trip

explanation: Knowing the exact arrival time helps the receiving staff prepare beds, equipment, and personnel ahead of time. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h6)

question: Why is early communication with the receiving facility critical during an evacuation?

options.A: To secure permission from local traffic police
options.B: To process insurance claims before the patient wakes
options.C: To allow the ambulance driver to rest midway
options.D: To allow the receiving team to prepare necessary resources

explanation: Alerting the destination hospital early ensures operating theatres, blood banks, and critical care units are ready upon arrival. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h6)

question: Which structured communication tool is commonly used during patient handover at the receiving facility?
explanation: Situation, Background, Assessment, and Recommendation provides an organized structure for passing critical patient details between clinicians. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h7)

question: What is the legal importance of handing over completed transit documentation to the receiving hospital?

options.A: It allows the ambulance driver to collect a bonus
options.B: It removes all future liability from the receiving doctor
options.C: It provides an official record of care given during transport
options.D: It guarantees the patient will be discharged within a week

explanation: Accurate records document every medication, fluid volume, and vital sign measured on the road, maintaining professional accountability. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h7)
